2025_137_2025_bod_elections_booklet.page:
**What it is**
The Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) 2025 Board of Directors election booklet, informational material for the Troy School District Board of Education meeting of Feb. 11, 2025. It reprints MASB Bylaws Article IV on membership, explains the election and email voting procedures, and prints election statements for thirteen candidates on pages 5-17, closing with MASB's mission and vision on page 18.

**Board composition**
The MASB Board of Directors is comprised of 23 members, including three at-large directors. Sixteen directors are elected from the eight regions, two from each region, and one director per group is elected from Groups V, VI and VII. The MASB President nominates an at-large director, subject to Board approval. Article VIII, Section 6 permits only one director from any one local or intermediate school district board; Article VIII, Section 8 declares an unopposed nominee elected without an election.

**Seats up in 2025** (one seat each, three-year terms unless noted)

| Seat | Term | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Region 1 | two-year | Unopposed - Kristen Cambensy, Marquette Area Public Schools |
| Region 3 | three-year | Unopposed - Rick Dernberger, Zeeland Public Schools and Ottawa Area ISD |
| Region 4 | three-year | Unopposed - John Tramontana, DeWitt Public Schools |
| Region 6 | one-year, open seat | Contested, online ballot |
| Region 7 | three-year | Contested, online ballot |
| Region 8 | three-year, open seat | Contested, online ballot |
| Group V | three-year | Unopposed - Stephen Hyer, Clarkston Community Schools |
| Group VI | three-year | Unopposed - Marc Siegler, Walled Lake Consolidated Schools |

**Voting procedure**
Each district received ONE ballot, emailed to its superintendent secretary of record on Friday, Jan. 24, 2025, and not forwardable. Ballots had to be cast and confirmed by 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 5, 2025. Unofficial results were to be posted on the voicemail at 517.327.5915 generally after 2 p.m. that day and emailed that afternoon; official results were to be approved at the March 14, 2025, Board of Directors' meeting. Questions: Cheryl Huffman, 517.327.5915, chuffman@masb.org.

**Campaign restrictions**
No local district or ISD funds may be used to campaign, and candidates may not use district email accounts to reach other board members; a personal account is required. Expenditure questions go to MASB Legal Counsel Brad Banasik, J.D., bbanasik@masb.org or 517.327.5929. Candidates receive an address file under a revokable license limited to election-related contact.

**Candidates** (booklet pages 5-17)
- Region 6, one-year term: TiAnna Harrison, Kalamazoo Public Schools; Elizabeth O'Dell, St. Joseph County ISD.
- Region 7: Guillermo Z. Lopez, Lansing School District (incumbent); Cory McLaughlin, Jefferson Schools; Jack Temsey, Eaton RESA.
- Region 8: Jason Babbage, Allen Park Public Schools; Anisha Hannah, Pontiac School District; Paul Kolin, Bloomfield Hills Schools; Roderick Means, Westwood Community School District; Randel Meisner, Fitzgerald Public Schools; Scott Wallace, Fraser Public Schools; Ursula (Wester) Rogers, Romulus Community Schools; Lisa Valerio-Nowc, Clintondale Community Schools.

**Membership groups by pupil membership**
Group I, all intermediate districts; Group II, 0-1,400; Group III, 1,401-2,500; Group IV, 2,501-5,000; Group V, 5,001-11,000; Group VI, 11,001-40,000; Group VII, more than 40,000. Regions follow intermediate school district boundaries; Region 8 comprises Macomb ISD, Oakland Schools and Wayne RESA.
2025_137_2025_bod_elections_booklet.verbose:
**Document and purpose**
The Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) 2025 Board of Directors election booklet, included in the Troy School District Board of Education's Feb. 11, 2025 materials. It reprints MASB Bylaws Article IV on membership, describes the 2025 election and email voting procedures beginning on page 4, and prints election statements and service profiles for thirteen candidates on pages 5 through 17; the region and group list appears on page 2 and the mission and vision on page 18. A note on the candidate list states that incumbents are bolded.

**Membership structure (Bylaws Article IV, Section 2)**
The board of education of any public school district in Michigan may become an active member. Active members are divided into eight regions designated by intermediate school district boundaries:
- Region 1: Copper Country ISD, Delta-Schoolcraft ISD, Dickinson-Iron ISD, Eastern Upper Peninsula ISD, Gogebic-Ontonagon ISD, Marquette-Alger RESA, Menominee County ISD.
- Region 2: Alpena-Montmorency-Alcona ESD, Charlevoix-Emmet ISD, Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle ESD, COOR ISD, Iosco RESA, Manistee ISD, Northwest Education Services, Wexford-Missaukee ISD.
- Region 3: Ionia County ISD, Kent ISD, Mecosta-Osceola ISD, Montcalm Area ISD, Muskegon Area ISD, Newaygo County RESA, Ottawa Area ISD, West Shore ESD.
- Region 4: Bay-Arenac ISD, Clare-Gladwin RESD, Clinton County RESA, Gratiot-Isabella RESD, Midland County ESA, Saginaw ISD, Shiawassee RESD.
- Region 5: Genesee ISD, Huron ISD, Lapeer County ISD, Sanilac ISD, St. Clair County RESA, Tuscola ISD.
- Region 6: Allegan Area ESA, Barry ISD, Berrien RESA, Branch ISD, Calhoun ISD, Heritage Southwest ISD, Kalamazoo RESA, St. Joseph County ISD, Van Buren ISD.
- Region 7: Eaton RESA, Hillsdale County ISD, Ingham ISD, Jackson County ISD, Lenawee ISD, Livingston ESA, Monroe County ISD, Washtenaw ISD.
- Region 8: Macomb ISD, Oakland Schools, Wayne RESA.
Members are also divided into seven groups by pupil membership: Group I, all intermediate districts; Group II, 0 to 1,400; Group III, 1,401 to 2,500; Group IV, 2,501 to 5,000; Group V, 5,001 to 11,000; Group VI, 11,001 to 40,000; Group VII, more than 40,000.

**Board composition and limitations**
The Board of Directors is comprised of 23 members, including three at-large directors. Sixteen directors are elected from the eight regions, two from each region, and one director per group is elected from Groups V, VI and VII; the MASB President nominates a member as an at-large director, subject to Board approval. Article VIII, Section 6 permits only one director from any one local or intermediate school district board, and Article VIII, Section 8 declares an unopposed nomination elected without an election for that group or region.

**Seats up and unopposed outcomes**
Eight seats were up, one seat each and three-year terms unless otherwise noted: Regions 1 (two-year term), 3, 4, 6 (open seat, one-year term), 7, 8 (open seat), and Groups V and VI. Five drew no opposition and no ballots were sent: Region 1, Kristen Cambensy, Marquette Area Public Schools; Region 3, Rick Dernberger, Zeeland Public Schools and Ottawa Area Intermediate School District; Region 4, John Tramontana, DeWitt Public Schools; Group V, Stephen Hyer, Clarkston Community Schools; Group VI, Marc Siegler, Walled Lake Consolidated Schools. Voting in Regions 6, 7 and 8 took place via online ballot.

**Voting procedures and deadlines**
Each district received ONE ballot, emailed to the superintendent secretary on record with MASB on Friday, Jan. 24, 2025; ballots cannot be forwarded. Completed ballots had to be cast and confirmed by the superintendent secretary by 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 5, 2025. Unofficial results were to be available on the voicemail recording at 517.327.5915 generally after 2 p.m. on the deadline date and emailed that afternoon. Official results were to be approved at the March 14, 2025, Board of Directors' meeting, which newly elected directors should plan to attend. Questions went to Cheryl Huffman at 517.327.5915 or chuffman@masb.org.

**Campaign rules**
No local district or ISD funds can be used to campaign, and a candidate may not use a school district email account to message other school board members, so a personal account must be used. Questions on what constitutes an expenditure of school district funds go to MASB Legal Counsel Brad Banasik, J.D., at bbanasik@masb.org or 517.327.5929. Each candidate receives an electronic file of physical and email addresses for the voting group or region under a revokable license limited to contacting school board members about the election.

**Region 6 candidates (one-year term)**
TiAnna Harrison, Kalamazoo Public Schools, Kalamazoo County (page 5), is Board President for the Kalamazoo Public Schools Board of Education, appointed in 2014 and reelected in 2020, and has served as Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer. She emphasizes state-level policies, equitable funding, and the mental and emotional well-being of students and staff. Profile: 10 years; offices of President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer; certification through Master Diamond. She signs as TiAnna L. Harrison, Trustee - Board of Education.
Elizabeth O'Dell, St. Joseph County ISD, St. Joseph County (page 6), has been an active St. Joseph County ISD member for 27 years, holding positions from member to president; her profile lists 27 years, offices of President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer, and certification through Master Diamond. She credits Past President Kathleen Moore, and cites the parent-teacher association, band and athletic booster clubs, the special education advisory committee, and service as an MASB delegate. She holds a bachelor's degree from Ball State University and a graduate degree from Western Michigan University, is retired CEO of St. Joseph County Community Mental Health, and volunteers with her church, American Red Cross Disaster Relief, as a substitute teacher, and through Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated.

**Region 7 candidates (three-year term)**
Guillermo Z. Lopez, Lansing School District, Ingham County (page 7), is marked INCUMBENT. He pledges attention to possible federal education funding changes, continued support for MASB's equity work and for districts that need training but cannot cover the cost, and cites the Region 7 newsletter. Profile: 24 years; offices of President and Treasurer.
Cory McLaughlin, Jefferson Schools, Monroe County (page 8), joined the Jefferson School Board in 2014 and prioritizes Career and Technical Education (CTE), advanced classes and special education. Profile: 11 years; MASB Certified Boardmember (CBA 101); offices of President and Secretary.
Jack Temsey, Eaton RESA, Eaton County (page 9), served the Potterville Public Schools Board of Education for eight years on the Policy, Community Relations and Technology Committees and as Secretary and Treasurer, and has been an Eaton RESA Trustee for eight years on the Building and Grounds and Finance and Audit Committees and as Secretary, Vice President and Treasurer, serving again as President. For MASB he has served on the Curriculum and Instruction Committee, the Government Relations Committee as Vice Chairman, and the Resolutions and Bylaws committee as Vice Chairman. Certification is listed through Master Platinum, earned via MASB's CBA program.

**Region 8 candidates (three-year term)**
Jason Babbage, Allen Park Public Schools, Wayne County (page 10), an alumnus and lifelong resident, holds a master's in automotive systems engineering and a bachelor's in mechanical engineering from U-M Dearborn and works at Ford Motor Company on exterior automotive lighting as a top expert in headlamp aim (HLA). He achieved his MASB Level 2 award of merit, has two children in Allen Park schools, and cites unfunded policies, declining enrollment, higher education standards, educational technology and sensory rooms. Profile: 2 years.
Anisha Hannah, Pontiac School District, Oakland County (page 11), is Director of Strategic Partnership & Initiatives with the Pontiac Collective Impact Partnership, developing initiatives for the City of Pontiac that support Oakland County's goal of 80 by 30. She has served as Board President with the City of Pontiac School Board of Education. Profile: 3 years; certification through Award of Distinction; offices of Vice President and Secretary.
Paul Kolin, Bloomfield Hills Schools, Oakland County (page 12), cites a background in Bloomfield Hills for the last 10 years and prior work as a teacher. Profile: 10 years; certification through Award of Distinction; offices of President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer.
Roderick Means, Westwood Community School District, Wayne County (page 13), a single parent of two young boys, coached little league baseball and football and served as a Cub and Boy Scout leader from Tiger Cub Coordinator to Cubmaster. For the last 20 years he has worked as an Application Developer at the University of Michigan Ann Arbor. He has served on MASB's Government Relations, Bylaws and Policy, and Board Leadership and Training committees and as an MASB Board Mentor. Profile: 28 years; certification through Master Platinum plus the President's Award; offices of President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer.
Randel Meisner, Fitzgerald Public Schools, Macomb County (page 14), lists concerns of sustainable funding, teacher retention, teacher shortages, full funding for special education, and offsetting the MPSERS cost. Experience: MISD Legislative Committee, MISD Budget Review, annual legislative strategic planning sessions, state Annual Leadership Conferences and National School Board Conferences; awarded the MASB President's Award. Profile: 12 years; certification through Master Platinum and President's Award; offices of Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer.
Scott Wallace, Fraser Public Schools (page 15), graduated from the district as did his three children. An Eagle Scout, he coached soccer and basketball and served four years as an officer on the Board of Directors for the Fraser Soccer Club. He has been President of the Fraser Public Schools Board of Education since 2022 and a board member since 2017, and served three years on the MASB legislative committee. Profile: 8 years; certification through Master Boardmember; offices of President, Vice President and Treasurer.
Ursula (Wester) Rogers, Romulus Community Schools, Wayne County (page 16), has worked as a substitute teacher, secretary, human resources professional and school board member, serving on policy, human resources, school improvement and curriculum committees, and has been involved with the Romulus Athletic Club for 24 years as treasurer and cheerleading coach for a youth football organization. Profile: 8 years; certification through Master Boardmember; offices of President, Secretary and Treasurer.
Lisa Valerio-Nowc, Clintondale Community Schools, Macomb County (page 17), has been a librarian for over thirty years as a School Librarian, Library Director of Baker College, and in public library leadership, and is currently Assistant Manager/Children's Librarian at the Chaney Branch of the Detroit Public Library. Profile: 2 years; office of Secretary.

**Mission and vision (page 18)**
Mission: to provide high-quality educational leadership services for all Michigan boards of education and to advocate for an equitable and exceptional public education that leads to improved outcomes for all students. Vision: a well-governed, effective public school for every Michigan student.
